Attribute: Division of Cancer Control and Population Sciences
Description: Conducts and supports an integrated program of the highest quality genetic, epidemiological, behavioral, social, applied, and surveillance cancer research.

According to the FY2004 Defense Appropriations Act, DOD is responsible for funding of several cancer research programs such as studies on breast, ovarian, and prostate cancer, leukemia, and myeloproliferative disease.

One of the agencies of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services. It assures the safety of foods and cosmetics, and the safety and efficacy of pharmaceuticals, biological products, radiation emitting products, medical devices, and also, animal feed and drugs.
A biotechnology company which develops and manufactures genomic analysis diagnostics based on next-generation sequencing technology for detection of solid and circulating cancers.

The Federal Government's principal agency for cancer research. NCI conducts, coordinates, and funds cancer research, training, health information dissemination, and other programs with respect to the cause, diagnosis, prevention, and treatment of cancer. Part of the National Institutes of Health.
The primary agency of the U.S. federal government responsible for biomedical and public health research, comprising multiple institutes and centers including the National Cancer Institute.

A division of the National Institutes of Health, it is the world's largest biomedical library. Its mission is to enable biomedical research, support health care and public health, and promote healthy behavior.

Formed in Jan, 2001 by the merger of the Division of Clinical Sciences and the Division of Basic Sciences, the Center for Cancer Research is the largest component of the National Cancer Institute's Intramural Research Program.

Attribute: Purdue University Center for Cancer Research
Description: The mission of the Purdue University Center for Cancer Research is to promote discovery in the areas of biological phenomena, new chemical entities, and new technology that leads to the development of innovative instrumentation, new diagnostic tools, and novel therapeutics.

The mission of the UNC Lineberger Comprehensive Cancer Center is to reduce cancer occurrence and death through research, treatment, training, and outreach. Designated as an NCI cancer center in 1975 and as a comprehensive cancer center in 1990.

The mission of the Georgetown Lombardi Comprehensive Cancer Center is to improve the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of cancer through innovative basic science, clinical research, patient care, community outreach, and the training of cancer specialists of the future.
National Clinical Trials Network (NCI)
Proteogenomic Translational Research Center

Attribute: Evelyn H. Lauder Founder’s Fund for Metastatic Breast Cancer Research
Description: An international, multi-year collaboration to understand the molecular basis of metastasis in real people in real time. It aims to identify the molecular changes that occur as breast cancer evolves from a localized disease to one that has metastasized.

A program at Johns Hopkins University, supported by the National Cancer Institute, that supports the genetics community by providing high-quality, cutting edge genomics services and technologies in order to expand the understanding of disease and catalyze discoveries that translate to patient care.

A not-for-profit, international organization committed to improving the quality of life for transplant candidates, transplant recipients, families of transplant candidates and recipients, and families of organ and tissue donors.

A charitable organization that funds development and delivery of next-generation therapies, the leverage of data to identify optimal and more personalized treatment approaches, and empowers myeloma patients and the broader community with information and resources.

A charitable organization that is the largest non-profit funding source for blood cancer research around the world. It also provides free information and support services for patients and their families, and is an advocate for those seeking access to quality, affordable, coordinated care.

Attribute: Center for Biomedical Informatics and Information Technology
Description: A National Cancer Institute (NCI) Center that works to provide NCI staff and the cancer research community with the data science, information technology, and data sharing tools they need to advance the knowledge of cancer.
The mission of the Knight Cancer Institute is to translate discoveries into better ways to diagnose, prevent, and treat cancer. It became an NCI-designated Cancer Center in 1997.

A joint research venture of MIT and Harvard, established in 2004 to improve human health by using genomics to advance an understanding of the biology and treatment of human disease, and to help lay the groundwork for a new generation of therapies.
